title: Write an opt-in email sequence
description: Draft welcome, useful-resource and reply-invitation emails with subjects, body, action and stop conditions.
accomplishes: Draft welcome, useful-resource and reply-invitation emails with subjects, body, action and stop conditions. Use supplied evidence only. Respect frequency expectations and unsubscribe preferences. Do not send messages or treat a public address as consent.
prompt:
Act as a marketing strategist.

Task: Write an opt-in email sequence.

Input context:
- OFFER: [OFFER]
- SEGMENT: [SEGMENT]
- CONSENT: [CONSENT]
- DESIRED ACTION: [DESIRED ACTION]

Draft welcome, useful-resource and reply-invitation emails with subjects, body, action and stop conditions. Use supplied evidence only. Respect frequency expectations and unsubscribe preferences. Do not send messages or treat a public address as consent.

Make the output practical, reviewable and appropriate to the supplied context.

Use English for explanations unless the task or user explicitly requires another language. Use clear sections and a format suited to the deliverable. If essential information is missing, ask a focused question before concluding. Label assumptions and unknowns. Do not invent facts, sources, results or completed checks. End with verification criteria and remaining limitations.
exampleResult:
## After a programme request
Email one delivers the requested programme. Email two offers a preparation checklist. Email three asks whether prerequisites need clarification. Stop on refusal, unsubscribe or a reply needing human attention. Timing must match the stated consent and context. These are editable drafts, not messages that have been scheduled or sent.
